title: fix #936 store root tablet file list in Zookeeper
description:
I just finished writing and testing this.  I plan to go back over it and review it myself after taking a bit of break from it.  Posting it as a draft in case anyone else wants to take a look.  The following overall changes were made :

  * List of root tablet files are now stored in ZK
  * The root tablets logical time is now stored in ZK
 * The compactID and flushID are now stored in ZK (should help with fixing #798)
  * List of root tablet GC candidates are now stored in ZK
  * Accumulo GC was modified to process root tablet files
  * A lot of specialized code for managing the list of root tablet files was removed or moved to upgrade code.

comments.body:
I really like this approach of setting something in the value.  I had hoped everything related to this change could be isolated to the upgrade code, but not that I am looking at the code I see that it can't.  While the upgrade code is running two other processes could also happen concurrently.   The Accumulo GC may be running and Metadata tablets could be compacting.  The Accumulo GC would see the old and new del markers.  Metadata table compactions could write out new delete markers which this code could corrupt.

One possible solution to this would be to always put something in the value for new style delete markers, which you mentioned doing in #1344.  Then AMPLE code could always ignore old style and new delete markers written out during upgrade would not be modified.

title: Fix GcMetricsIT test when multiple IT tests run
description: The test previously did not account for metrics that were published from previous runs or if multiple IT tests were run without cleaning the target directory.  The metrics are read from a file that is appended, so previous test values could cause test failures - with this change, the GcMetricsIT test ignores the first line and then processes the subsequent updates generated during the test.

issue_comments.author: EdColeman
issue_comments.body: I've been working on the back-port and being that the underlying code in this test is shared with the fate concurrency and fate metrics, I've been running the 3 IT tests each time, and that's when this began to fail. It was fine stand-alone and in the IDE.  Being that the file is created by the metrics subsystem, it seemed preferable to treat the metrics subsystem as the "owner" and then just deal with it.
